title: confiture migrate verify --format json
description: Runtime-correctness verification of applied migrations via .verify.sql sidecars (VerifyAllResult.to_dict). The fraisier migration adapter reads ok and each results[].{version,name,status,error}. Through 1.11.0 there was no ok field and the rule was ok ⇔ failed_count == 0; that inference is wrong for a ledger-less run under --allow-uninitialized, where failed_count is 0 because nothing ran. 1.12.0 adds ok (ledger_present && failed_count == 0) and was_skipped, matching verify-checksums (#311). A migration with no .verify.sql is reported with status "no_file", and one whose sidecar holds no statement yet with status "skipped"; both count in skipped_count, never failed_count. A crash (config/DB error) emits the error envelope (error-envelope.schema.json) instead of this shape.

ok.description: True when verification actually happened and nothing failed: ledger_present && failed_count == 0. Read THIS, not failed_count alone (1.12.0, #311). Until 1.12.0 this payload carried no ok at all and the contract said ok ⇔ failed_count == 0 — which is 0 on a ledger-less run under --allow-uninitialized for the trivial reason that nothing ran, so a conforming consumer read success from a run that verified nothing. failed_count itself was never wrong; the inference drawn from it was. Same field, same meaning, as verify-checksums' ok: two neighbouring commands answering "I could not verify anything" differently is a trap of its own.

was_skipped.description: True when the run verified nothing because the ledger was absent — only reachable under --allow-uninitialized, since otherwise the same state raises PRECON_1001 (exit 2). Always present, never absent-on-success, so a consumer never has to branch before it can read it (1.12.0, #311).

verified_count.description: Number of applied migrations whose .verify.sql passed.

failed_count.description: Number of applied migrations whose .verify.sql assertion failed. 0 is NOT by itself a success signal: a ledger-less run under --allow-uninitialized has 0 because nothing ran. Read ok, which is ledger_present && failed_count == 0 (1.12.0, #311).

skipped_count.description: Number of applied migrations that were not verified: no .verify.sql sidecar (status "no_file"), or a sidecar holding no statement yet (status "skipped", 1.12.0). Neither is a failure and neither is a verification.

ledger_present.description: Whether the migration ledger table (tracking_table, default tb_confiture) exists. False means the database has no recorded migrations at all — typically built from schema files rather than migrated — and is only emitted under --allow-uninitialized, since without that flag the absent ledger raises PRECON_1001 (exit 2). Distinct from a present-but-empty ledger, which reports true with total_applied 0. Added in 0.37.0; not required, so payloads from earlier versions remain valid.

name.description: Migration name (may equal the version when no name was recorded).

status.description: Outcome: "verified", "failed", "no_file" (no sidecar), or "skipped" (a sidecar with no statement in it — what `migrate generate` writes beside a new migration, so it is the state most sidecars are in on the day they are created; 1.12.0, #311). The adapter treats anything other than "failed" as ok.

actual_value.description: First column of the first row the .verify.sql query returned; null when no file or no row.

verify_file.description: Path to the .verify.sql sidecar; null when none.

error.description: Failure detail when status is "failed"; null otherwise.

parser.description: What parsed the SQL behind this payload (0.50.0): the installed pglast release and the PostgreSQL grammar major it embeds.
